- [LCYC.6.1] **Slot-value refinement.** A rule that matches
  `Alert a where a.severity > 5` and emits an
  `Alert` with `severity: 7` is technically
  self-referential but may not be infinite — it
  depends on whether re-matching happens with
  a value that would re-trigger. The compiler
  applies a **literal-equality cycle-breaking
  check to every edge of the rule graph**: if every
  non-negated LHS pattern the target rule has for
  the schema carries a `binding.slot == X`
  where-clause constraint that the source rule's
  RHS emit violates (emits `slot: Y` with literal
  `Y ≠ X`), the edge is dropped. The emit provably
  cannot satisfy that LHS, so it cannot close a
  loop through it.
  This handles the common "kind flip" pattern
  (match `kind == "enter"`, emit `kind: "leave"`)
  whether the flip sits on one rule or is spread
  across several, without opening up genuine
  infinite loops. Non-literal expressions
  (arithmetic, slot references) remain strict.
